description: Principality of Hungary (895–1000), nomadic Magyar confederation that settled the Carpathian Basin after migrating from the Pontic steppe; the Battle of Lechfeld (955) ended Magyar raids into western Europe and opened the path to Christianisation under Géza and Stephen I, whose 1000 CE papal coronation transformed the confederation into a Christian feudal kingdom integrated into European diplomatic networks.

temporal.notes: Stub: dates from GeoJSON basemap years 700–1000

lifecycle_phases.description: Ugrian-speaking Magyar tribes migrated westward from the Ural region; settled in the Pontic steppe before the Pecheneg invasion.
Magyar tribes crossed the Carpathians into the Pannonian plain (895) after Pechenegs destroyed their steppe homeland.
Magyar cavalry raided throughout western Europe, reaching Spain and southern Italy; finally stopped at the Battle of Lechfeld (955).
Christianisation under Géza and Stephen I; Hungary established as a Christian kingdom (1000).

rise_factors.description: Magyar horse archers were among the most mobile warriors in Europe; effective across vast raid distances.
The Carpathian Basin provided a defensible base with rich agricultural potential after settlement.

decline_factors.description: Otto I's victory at Lechfeld (955) ended the raiding era and forced Magyar political transformation.
Conversion to Christianity ended the mobile raiding economy and required integration into feudal European norms.
